qa_pairs.instruction: What is the purpose of Directory Scopes in the Google Apps driver?
qa_pairs.output: In the Google Apps driver, Directory Scopes define the specific Google APIs that the driver is allowed to access. They are required for operations such as managing groups, users, organizational units, and other directory data. Providing the correct scopes ensures the driver can perform its functions while complying with Google’s security model.

qa_pairs.instruction: How do you correctly format the list of authorized scopes for the Google Apps driver?
qa_pairs.output:
To format the authorized scopes for the Google Apps driver:
1. Open a plain‑text editor (do not use a word processor or rich‑text editor).
2. Copy the scope URLs from the DirectoryScopes.txt file bundled with the driver.
3. Paste them into the editor ensuring there is **no extra formatting** or hidden characters.
4. Place all scopes on a **single line**, separated only by commas.
5. Save the file and use it when authorizing the service account as described in section 2.2.3 – Configuring API and Service Account.
Following these steps prevents clipboard‑related failures caused by hidden formatting.

qa_pairs.instruction: What are the authorized scopes required by the Google Apps driver?
qa_pairs.output:
The Google Apps driver requires the following authorized scopes (comma‑separated on a single line):

https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group,
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group.member,
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.orgunit,
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user,
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user.alias,
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user.security,
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.userschema,
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.profile,
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email,
http://www.google.com/m8/feeds,
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/contacts.readonly,
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/apps.groups.settings,
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.rolemanagement,
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.settings.basic,
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.settings.sharing,
https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.labels,
https://apps-apis.google.com/a/feeds/emailsettings/2.0/

qa_pairs.instruction: Why might authentication fail when authorizing scopes for the Google Apps driver, and how can you fix it?
qa_pairs.output: Authentication failures often occur when the scope list is not pure plain text. If you copy and paste the scopes from a web page, PDF, or rich document, hidden characters (such as smart quotes, non‑breaking spaces, or line‑break markers) can be introduced. These extra characters cause Google to reject the scope string. To fix the issue, recreate the scope list in a plain‑text editor, ensure all scopes are on one line separated only by commas, and avoid any formatting or invisible characters before re‑authorizing the service account.

qa_pairs.instruction: Summarize the key points about configuring authorized scopes for the Google Apps driver.
qa_pairs.output: The Google Apps driver requires a specific set of Google API scopes listed in DirectoryScopes.txt. These scopes must be entered as plain text, on a single line, comma‑separated, using a simple text editor. Copy‑paste from rich sources can add hidden characters and cause authorization failures. Always reference the bundled DirectoryScopes.txt (and any driver patches) for the most up‑to‑date list.
